Apple Podcasts has long been my go-to podcast app, but for years I've had one major complaint about its core "Up Next" queue feature. The good news is that iOS 27.2 finally brings a fix.

iOS 27.2 splits Apple Podcasts' "Up Next" queue into two sections: "New Episodes" and "Continue Listening"

There's a lot to love about Apple Podcasts. Transcripts and auto-generated chapters are two killer features that keep it as my go-to app. I've also really enjoyed all the recent video-related upgrades.

But for years, Apple Podcasts' core "Up Next" queue has been making me want to switch to another app.

I've written before about why the "Up Next" feature feels broken. In short:

  • It doesn't give you a great overview of what shows you have ready to listen to
  • Some episodes are too easy to lose, even if you only listened to half

However, I'm happy to report that iOS 27.2 brings a long-awaited revision to "Up Next." The solution is to split it into two separate parts:

  • New Episodes
  • Continue Listening

At the very top of the app is "New Episodes," which looks and functions similarly to the original "Up Next." The difference is that, as the name suggests, it only shows the latest episode from each of your followed shows.

"Continue Listening" sits just below, serving as a central hub for all the episodes you've started but haven't finished.

Top comment from Nutmac

Queue management is still a mess, and the lack of cross-device syncing is baffling.

Together, these two sections address all of my biggest gripes with the "Up Next" queue.

I can see all my new content at a glance, and because any episode I start listening to appears in "Continue Listening," I'll never miss an episode again. There are still a few minor quibbles, but these changes alone fix my main issues with "Up Next."

If you haven't tried Apple Podcasts in a while, iOS 27.2 is the perfect time to give it another shot.

Do you use Apple's Podcasts app or a different podcast app? Let us know in the comments.
